scams.name: Fake Terracotta Army Site & 'Shortcut' Tour
scams.description:
You are at Xi'an Railway Station or your hotel lobby looking for transport to the Terracotta Warriors. A taxi driver or a booth agent offers a "Terracotta Army tour" for ¥150 and the destination name sounds plausible. The real Emperor Qin Shi Huang's Mausoleum Site Museum is at Lintong, 35 kilometers east of Xi'an — a specific address that differs from dozens of "Qin Museum" or "Warriors Heritage Park" venues along the same road, built specifically to intercept tourists who do not know the difference.

In the fake-site version the driver pulls up to a venue marked "Terracotta Warriors." Inside are mass-produced replica warriors and general exhibits; the entry fee is ¥100–¥200. Visitors realize they never reached the official archaeological site only after comparing photos with other travelers. In the shopping-stop tour version the ¥150 day-trip price works because 80% of the itinerary is mandatory stops at jade factories, tea "museums," and silk "factories" — each paying the guide 20–30% commission — with the actual Terracotta Army visit compressed to 60–90 minutes.

Take Tourist Bus Line 5 (游5) from Xi'an Railway Station East Plaza — ¥8 one-way, every 20 minutes, and it terminates at the official museum gate . Book entry tickets (¥120 adult) at the official WeChat mini-program or Trip.com with the correct address already filled in. For a guided tour, use Viator or GetYourGuide and require "zero shopping stops" in writing before paying; honest full-day tours cost ¥300–¥500 per person.
scams.avoidance: Take Tourist Bus Line 5 (游5) from Xi'an Railway Station East Plaza — ¥8, 1 hour, every 20 min Book entry ticket (¥120 adult) at the official WeChat mini-program 'Qin Shi Huang Di Ling Bowu Yuan' or Trip.com For guided tours, use Viator, GetYourGuide, or hotel Ctrip partnership; verify ZERO shopping stops in writing Reject any tour booth at Xi'an Railway Station or hotel lobby offering 'discount Terracotta tour' under ¥200 Confirm the destination as 'Emperor Qin Shi Huang's Mausoleum Site Museum' — nothing else
scams.location: Outside Xi'an city center on the road to Lintong; fake 'Terracotta Museum' venues along the route, hotel lobby tour-booth referrals
scams.tldr: Taxis and cheap tour operators in Xi'an deliver tourists to fake "Qin Museum" replica venues 35 km short of the real site, charging ¥100–¥200 entry for mass-produced warrior replicas — a related variant books tourists onto ¥150 tours that spend 80% of the day at commission-paying shopping stops.

scams.name: Muslim Quarter Tourist-Menu & 'Famous' Food Stall Overcharge
scams.description:
Beiyuanmen — the main pedestrian street just north of the Drum Tower — is Xi'an's most-photographed food-tourism zone. Every sign is in English and Chinese, every stall has a laminated photo menu and a person outside gesturing you in. The scene looks like the definitive local food experience. Locals eat one street over, at stalls with posted prices and no English solicitation.

Prices on Beiyuanmen run 2–3x what the same dishes cost at residential stalls a block off the tourist strip: ¥30–¥50 for yangrou paomo (lamb bread soup) versus ¥15–¥20 elsewhere; ¥40–¥60 for biangbiang noodles that cost ¥15–¥25; ¥35 per lamb skewer that should be ¥5–¥10. A separate pushcart scam targets tourists at the dried-fruit displays: a vendor cuts a "small" piece of Xinjiang dried-fruit cake and weighs it — the piece turns out to be 200+ grams at ¥12 per gram, producing a bill of ¥2,000 or more for what appeared to be a snack.

Walk one street off Beiyuanmen to Huajue Xiang or Xiyangshi Street before choosing any stall, and always ask "duo shao qian" (how much) before the vendor starts cutting or serving . Community-verified honest venues include Yongxing Fang food court (posted prices), Lao Sun Jia (yangrou paomo ¥45), and Jia San Guantang Baozi (soup dumplings ¥30). Never buy Xinjiang cake from a pushcart; if you want to try it, buy a pre-packaged version at a supermarket for ¥5–¥15.
scams.avoidance: Eat one street off Beiyuanmen: Huajue Xiang, Xiyangshi Street, or Yongxing Fang food court Community-verified venues: Lao Sun Jia (yangrou paomo ¥45), Jia San (soup dumplings ¥30), Yongxing Fang (posted prices) NEVER buy 'Xinjiang cake' from a pushcart — supermarket pre-packaged versions are ¥5–¥15 Confirm 'duo shao qian' (how much) BEFORE the vendor starts cutting or serving Reject any tout pulling you toward a restaurant with English-photo menus
scams.location: Muslim Quarter (Beiyuanmen / North Gate Market) main street, around Drum Tower south entrance, Huimin Street
scams.tldr: Tourist-facing stalls on Beiyuanmen (Muslim Quarter main street) charge ¥30–¥60 for yangrou paomo and biangbiang noodles that cost ¥15–¥25 one street over, while pushcart vendors run a "Xinjiang cake" weight scam that turns a snack-sized piece into a ¥2,000+ bill.

scams.name: Xi'an Airport (XIY) Taxi Overcharge & Station Touts
scams.description:
You clear immigration at Xi'an Xianyang International Airport (XIY) after a long flight. XIY is 40 kilometers northwest of the city center and the terminal exit is where unlicensed drivers concentrate. A man in a polo approaches before you reach the official taxi sign: "Taxi? Fixed price 400 yuan, very fast." He looks professional and the offer sounds convenient.

The legitimate metered fare from XIY to Xi'an city center is ¥120–¥160 for the 45-minute ride. The tout's "fixed price" of ¥300–¥400 is 2–3x the meter rate and comes with no accountability — no registered vehicle number, no receipt, and no recourse if the driver takes a longer route or adds fees at the destination. A separate Xi'an airport scam involves a stranger asking to borrow your phone: "I lost mine in a taxi, I just need to call one number." They then walk away with it, or use it to access a WeChat Pay account before returning it.

Walk past anyone soliciting inside the terminal and take airport Metro Line 14 (¥17, 70 minutes) or the airport shuttle bus (¥25, 60 minutes) to Xi'an Railway Station — both are scam-proof . If you need a car, install DiDi before flying and order at the official rideshare pickup zone; for a licensed street taxi, say "da biao" (打表 — run the meter) before boarding and photograph the license plate from the rear windscreen. Never hand your unlocked phone to a stranger at the airport for any reason.
scams.avoidance: Install DiDi before flying with international number; use at official rideshare pickup zone Take airport Metro Line 14 (¥17, 70 min) or shuttle bus (¥25, 60 min) for scam-proof option If licensed taxi, say 'da biao' (打表) before boarding; confirm ¥120–¥160 range NEVER hand your unlocked phone to any stranger at the airport Photograph taxi plate number from rear windscreen on entering
scams.location: Xi'an Xianyang International Airport (XIY) arrivals, Xi'an Railway Station East Plaza, Xi'an North High-Speed Rail Station
scams.tldr: Unlicensed taxi touts at Xi'an Xianyang Airport (XIY) intercept arriving tourists inside the terminal with "fixed price 300–400 yuan" offers that are 2–3x the legitimate metered ¥120–¥160 fare — a separate phone-borrowing scam at arrivals adds a parallel theft risk.

scams.name: Bell Tower & Drum Tower Area Pickpockets
scams.description:
Xi'an's historic core draws massive tour-group traffic — particularly between 10 AM and 2 PM when buses arrive at Bell Tower and the City Wall. The Bell Tower underground pedestrian passage connecting all four sides, the Drum Tower's south entrance where food crowds and tour groups converge at the Muslim Quarter border, and the Yongningmen (South Gate) ticket office queue are all high-density zones where personal space collapses briefly and repeatedly throughout the day.

Pickpockets here are opportunistic rather than organized: they move through the same crowd flow as tourists, exploit the moment when a photo is being taken or a map is being checked, and target phones in back pockets or outer backpack compartments. The City Wall bike-rental station is a secondary zone where deposits are handled in cash and the manual transaction creates a distraction. The Big Wild Goose Pagoda square during the evening fountain show draws similar compressed crowds.

Wear your bag across your front with the zipper facing your body at Bell Tower, Drum Tower, and the City Wall South Gate ticket queue — a bag on your back in a compressed tour-group crowd is accessible without you noticing. Keep your phone in a zipped inner pocket rather than a back pocket or outer backpack compartment. Carry only ¥200 and one card; leave your passport and backup card in the hotel safe. If theft occurs, call 110 and China's English-language consumer-protection line 12315 within 24 hours.
scams.avoidance: Wear crossbody bag zipped in front during Bell Tower / Drum Tower / City Wall walks Never place phone in back pocket or outer backpack compartment Carry only ¥200 + one card; passport + backup in hotel safe Bike rental at City Wall is ¥45 for 100 min (published) — verify deposit returned in full If theft occurs, call 110 and 12315 (English-line consumer protection) within 24 hours
scams.location: Xi'an Bell Tower and Drum Tower squares, City Wall South Gate tourist crowd, Xi'an Ancient City Wall bike-rental area
scams.tldr: Pickpockets work the Bell Tower underground passage, Drum Tower Muslim Quarter entrance, and City Wall South Gate ticket queue during tour-group arrival peaks, using crowd compression to lift phones from back pockets and unzip bags from behind.

scams.name: Jade 'Factory' Forced-Shopping Tour Stops
scams.description:
You book a full-day Terracotta Army tour at your hotel lobby or a booth near Xi'an Railway Station for ¥150–¥200 per person. The itinerary lists the warriors, Huaqing Hot Spring, and "a traditional jade demonstration." The price sounds fair for a long day. The guide collects the group at 8 AM and the bus heads east toward Lintong.

The "jade demonstration" stop is a 90-minute session at a private retail operation presented as a "government-certified jade museum." The certification displayed is a standard Chinese business license — which every business holds — that the guide presents as state endorsement of quality. Sales pressure is systematic: staff work one-on-one with tourists, prices drop rapidly to create urgency, and the jade sold is typically serpentine or dyed quartz, not imperial jadeite, at 5–20x market price. The guide's commission is 20–30% of anything you buy. The identical pattern runs in Beijing and Chengdu.

Book only tours with "zero shopping stops" confirmed in writing before paying — licensed small-group operators on Viator, GetYourGuide, or hotel-partnership Ctrip tours will provide this in writing . Honest full-day tours without shopping stops cost ¥300–¥500 per person; anything priced below ¥250 economically requires shopping-stop commissions to function. If you are already on a tour that stops at a jade factory, simply wait out the 45–60 minutes without buying — the guide cannot legally compel purchases.
scams.avoidance: Book only tours with 'ZERO shopping stops' verified in writing before paying Use licensed operators: Viator, GetYourGuide, Tiqets, or hotel-partner Ctrip tours Expect ¥300–¥500 per person for honest full-day tours; anything lower includes shopping If already on a shopping-stop tour, simply don't buy — wait out the 45–60 min stop Report shopping-stop tours to 12315 (consumer protection English line) for documentation
scams.location: Along tour bus routes between Xi'an city center and Terracotta Warriors / Huaqing Hot Spring, 'government jade museums' bundled with Terracotta day trips
scams.tldr: Xi'an day-trip bus tours priced below ¥250 per person include mandatory 60–120 minute stops at "government-certified jade factories" and traditional Chinese medicine "museums" where the guide earns 20–30% commission — the jade sold is typically serpentine or dyed quartz marked up 5–20x market price.

scams.name: Tang Paradise / Huaqing Hot Spring 'Show' Ticket Scams
scams.description:
Xi'an offers three well-known cultural evening experiences: the Tang Dynasty Show at the Xi'an Hotel, the "Song of Everlasting Sorrow" musical at Huaqing Palace, and the Tang Paradise evening water show. All three are popular with visitors and genuinely worth attending. The ticket prices are public and fixed — but hotel concierges and street flyer touts at the venues exploit unfamiliarity with what the shows actually cost.

Hotel concierges push "exclusive" or "English-guided" show packages at ¥600–¥900 per person for shows whose direct ticket is ¥298–¥498. Street touts outside the venues sell "VIP" tickets at 1.5–2x face value for seats that are actually standard seating. A third variant is the "Dinner + Show" bundle: a mediocre buffet priced at ¥400 is added to the ticket, taking the total to ¥1,000 or more per person for an experience that costs ¥298 booked directly, with dinner at a nearby restaurant for ¥100.

Book the Tang Dynasty Show, Huaqing Palace evening show, or Tang Paradise water show directly through the venue's WeChat mini-program or Trip.com at published rates of ¥298–¥498 — the direct booking apps are in English and take five minutes. Ignore hotel-concierge packages above ¥600 per person; all are commission markups on fixed-price tickets. Metro Line 2 serves the Tang Paradise area for ¥5; Huaqing Palace is reached by Lintong tourist bus (¥8) plus a short taxi for Huaqing Hot Spring.
scams.avoidance: Book Tang Dynasty Show or Huaqing Palace show directly via venue WeChat mini-program or Trip.com Legitimate rates: ¥298 standard, ¥398 VIP, ¥598 dinner+show Ignore hotel-concierge packages over ¥600 per person — all are commission markups Metro Line 2 serves Tang Paradise area (¥5); Lintong tourist bus ¥8 + taxi ¥20 for Huaqing Palace For evening return, use DiDi (app-regulated) rather than venue taxi touts
scams.location: Tang Paradise (曲江大唐芙蓉园) evening water show area, Huaqing Palace hot spring evening shows, hotel-concierge Tang Dynasty Show packages
scams.tldr: Hotel concierges and street touts sell Xi'an's Tang Dynasty Show, Huaqing Palace evening performance, and Tang Paradise water show at ¥600–¥900 per person — 2–3x the ¥298–¥498 rates available directly from venue booking apps and Trip.com.

scams.name: Xi'an Tea Ceremony / Tea House Invitation
scams.description:
You are in Bell Tower plaza or near the Drum Tower approach when someone in good English steps in: "Hello, we are students at Xi'an Jiaotong University — may we practice English with you?" or "Excuse me, could you help us take a photo?" The conversation is natural and unhurried. Within twenty minutes a "traditional Shaanxi tea ceremony nearby" comes up — a chance to experience local culture before heading back to the hotel.

The venue is a short walk to a quiet side street north or east of the Drum Tower. Tea is served — the tea itself is real — and the setting feels authentic. The bill arrives: ¥2,000 to ¥5,000 per person for a 30-minute tasting. The "students" are no longer in the room. Staff present a laminated rate card listing per-cup and per-pot fees; the tea is priced 30–80x the residential rate. Police are historically unhelpful because you appeared to attend willingly; credit-card chargeback and a 12315 report are the practical remedies.

Any stranger who approaches at Bell Tower, Drum Tower, the Muslim Quarter entrance, or Yongningmen Gate and steers toward "tea," "cultural experience," or a "Muslim Quarter tour" within twenty minutes is running this scam — the script is identical across Xi'an, Beijing, and Shanghai. Say "bu yao xie xie" and keep moving. For genuine Xi'an tea culture, the Defuxiang tea market southwest of Bell Tower has posted prices and no solicitation; alternatively, ask your hotel to recommend a verified teahouse with an English-language menu.
scams.avoidance: Walk past any stranger approaching at Bell Tower, Drum Tower, or Muslim Quarter entrance Never accept 'cultural experience' or 'tea ceremony' invitations from strangers For genuine Xi'an tea, visit Defuxiang tea market (posted prices) or hotel-verified venues Pay with credit card for chargeback leverage if trapped Call 12315 (English-line) and 110 (police) for both scam reports
scams.location: Bell Tower plaza, Drum Tower approach, Muslim Quarter entrance, around tourist-heavy Yong Ning Gate
scams.tldr: English-speaking "students" near Bell Tower and Drum Tower invite tourists to a "traditional Shaanxi tea ceremony" within twenty minutes of meeting, then present bills of ¥2,000–¥5,000 per person for a 30-minute tasting in a side-street venue that costs ¥100–¥200 at a legitimate teahouse.
